persons.name: Heisenberg
persons.digest:
Heisenberg's day centered largely on **Micron**: he explains that the company's gross margin expansion slowed quarter by quarter (+18.4, +10.2, +2.2 points) and that its own Q1'27 guidance shows -0.8 points for the first time. In his view, for a cyclical stock the price looks at the direction of margins rather than their level; a forward P/E that looks like about 4x is misleading because it is calculated on inflated margins. Technically, he gives $450-500 as the next zone if there is no sustained hold above $800-850; the peak ($1,213) was seen the day after the Q3 earnings.

He hopes those who bought **SanDisk**, **Micron** and similar names at the top eventually profit too, but adds that it shouldn't take months. He says a trade in a chip hardware basket at 3-5% risk "worked out nicely"; he also shared, without comment, Paradotor's claim that **Brent crude** will reach $225 in 21 days.

items.title: Micron's margin expansion rate is fading
items.summary: Micron's gross margin gains were +18.4, +10.2 and +2.2 points quarter over quarter, and the company's own Q1'27 guidance shows -0.8 points for the first time, meaning the company itself expects contraction. Because a cyclical stock's price looks at the direction of margins, a stock priced for continued expansion tends to fall to more reasonable multiples once the direction turns. The stock peaked ($1,213) the day after the Q3 earnings; in September price approached the peak while volume didn't even reach half the June peak, which is a classic Wyckoff distribution. He says this doesn't mean it will sink, only that it deserves a lower valuation, and notes he has been writing the same thing since July.

assets.note: Margin expansion rate is slowing and guidance shows contraction for the first time; the $1,213 peak came the day after Q3 earnings.

items.title: Zones of $800-850 and $450-500 for Micron
items.summary: He says the liquidation volume at the support zone makes it an obvious long, and that if the reaction there doesn't hold above the 200-day average and the prior S/R zone of $800-850, the next zone is $450-500. He adds there was a volume divergence at the top technically and four quarters of margin contraction fundamentally.

assets.note: If no sustained hold above $800-850, the next zone is $450-500.

items.title: Micron's forward P/E is misleading
items.summary: Annualizing the $38 EPS in Q1'27 guidance puts Micron at about 4x P/E, but that profit is calculated on an 86% gross margin; in the prior two cycles peak margins were 45-59%. He says that for a cyclical stock the P/E is usually most expensive when it looks lowest.

assets.note: The ~4x P/E is computed on an inflated 86% margin; margins are no longer rising.

items.title: Selling into rallies and rotation
items.summary: Quoting his own older tweet, he reminds that the probability of index-carrying stocks carrying the index again after long drawdowns is 12%. He says he hopes those who bought SanDisk, Micron and similar names at the top eventually profit, that there may be rotation back into them after summer but he doesn't know if it will be to the extent expected. He writes that what he bought from the 780 support is still held and that he sold half of it each time people got excited again on rallies.

assets.note: Those who bought at the top shouldn't need months to profit; the rotation expectation is limited.

persons.name: Defiant Gatekeeper
persons.digest:
Defiant Gatekeeper groups this week's events under three headings: the AI narrative cracking, everything falling including oil and yields, and the ball returning to the Fed's court. The weekly drop was 2.7% for the S&P 500 and 3.4% for the Nasdaq, while the semiconductor index lost another 12% in a week. In his view the damage concentrated in chipmakers (**Micron** and **AMD** about 17%, **Nvidia** about 9%), while chip buyers **Microsoft**, **Amazon** and **Google** fell less; the causes are post-election fear over data center approvals and year-end positioning.

Oil fell 13% on the week, and he ties the drop in yields and inflation expectations to expectations of an exit from the war. On the Fed, the December hike odds that dipped Thursday returned to roughly 80% after Friday's jobs data; unless next week's CPI is weak he sees a December hike as the base case, adding that what matters most is what is said at the next FOMC.

items.title: AI narrative cracking
items.summary: Weekly market update: the S&P 500 fell 2.7%, the Nasdaq 3.4% and the Dow 0.9%; the semiconductor index lost 7.2% last week and 12% this week. Thursday was the S&P 500's worst day since April 2025 and about $2 trillion was wiped from the Nasdaq. The selling concentrated in chipmakers: Micron and AMD fell about 17% and Nvidia about 9%, while chip buyers Amazon fell about 2%, Google 3% and Microsoft 4%. He offers two explanations: fear that a Democratic Congress will slow data center approvals (one analyst puts about 30% of expected 2028 capacity at risk) and hedge funds taking profits before year-end; he stresses the 30% figure is an estimate and no actual bill exists. Oil fell about 13% on the week, its biggest weekly drop since 2022, with Brent near $95 on the Wednesday after the election; since inflation expectations fell too, he ties this to pricing of an exit from the war. On the Fed, December hike odds were ~70% last Friday, ~80% midweek and ~67% Thursday, and returned to ~80% after Friday's 165K jobs figure; Thursday's initial jobless claims of 189K were the lowest since 1969 and Hammack and Daly said they expect tighter policy. Unless next week's CPI is weak, he sees a December hike as the base case.

persons.name: wallstengine
